task.title: Strength reconciliation: background-execution-assertion fix -- reviewed candidate ready

result.summary: Implemented the recommended next fix from the prior below-Task-layer diagnosis: protects ProductionEvidenceReviewAPI.resolveWorkoutReconciliation's whole submission (the original attempt and its existing, unchanged retry) with an iOS background-execution assertion (UIApplication.begin/endBackgroundTask, abstracted behind a testable BackgroundTaskScheduling protocol), so a brief app background/suspension transition can no longer have the in-flight request torn down by the OS before it finishes or fails cleanly. No retry logic was added or changed, per explicit instruction. The assertion ends exactly once regardless of ordering (success, thrown error, Task cancellation, or the OS expiration handler firing), guarded by a BackgroundTaskEndGuard against double-ending or leaking. Six new unit tests cover the wrapper's lifecycle in isolation, including a genuine RED check that caught and fixed a real bug in the test itself (a weak-self capture that made a fake expiration callback a silent no-op). Two new integration tests reproduce the exact Build 64 evidence end-to-end. Full regression: 1453/1453 unit tests, 13/13 UI tests. Independently fresh-context reviewed with no issues found, including independent re-execution of all 8 new tests. No build number bumped, no archive, no upload, no Founder confirmation attempt requested.

tests.summary: Full PhysiqueOSTests target: 1453/1453 passing (1445 prior + 8 new: 6 isolated lifecycle tests + 2 end-to-end integration tests). GoalsAcceptanceUITests 1/1, TrainingAcceptanceUITests 12/12 -- 13/13 UI tests passing, no regression. All runs after a clean build.

red_green.summary: Deliberately broke the BackgroundTaskEndGuard double-end guard and reran the relevant test: it initially still passed due to a real bug in the test (a weak-self capture in the fake scheduler making a late expiration callback a silent no-op) -- found and fixed the actual cause (changed the capture to a deliberate strong one, correct because the scheduler is the sole holder of that closure for exactly as long as the assertion is open). After that fix, breaking the guard produced a genuine failure ([1, 1] instead of [1]), and restoring it passed cleanly again.

review.summary: Independent fresh-context review (zero prior context) verified the diff directly against the code and independently re-ran all 8 new tests in the simulator. Confirmed correct locking with no deadlock risk on every path, no real retain-cycle risk from the strong-self capture, correct defer coverage of every exit path including Task cancellation, and that wrapping both the original attempt and its retry in a SINGLE assertion (not one each) is the right design since splitting them would reopen the exact vulnerability gap this fix targets. Confirmed no unintended changes elsewhere, including verifying the large project.pbxproj diff is purely positional file-ID renumbering from adding two new files, not any structural change. No issues found.

backlog: This fix targets the leading, most evidence-consistent hypothesis but cannot guarantee the next real attempt succeeds -- a genuine external network-path disruption at the same moment remains possible and is unaffected by this change.
